decision_reason: Agentic VLM/function-call mobile-manipulation framework; retain as modular-system context rather than a learned VLA action-policy report.
summary: OWMM-Agent uses multimodal scene and robot-state context to coordinate mobile manipulation through function calls. Its associated instruction tuning supports an agentic integration of perception, navigation, and manipulation components.

name: PaLM-E (contextual embodied VLM)
title: PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model
decision_reason: Embodied multimodal language model for reasoning and high-level planning; not an action-policy contribution under the selected boundary.
summary: PaLM-E incorporates visual observations and continuous sensor information into an embodied language model. It supports multimodal reasoning and high-level robot planning.

name: PerAct (language-conditioned 3D policy)
title: Perceiver-Actor: A Multi-Task Transformer for Robotic Manipulation
decision_reason: Language-conditioned 3D action-policy precursor first reported in 2022, outside January 2023 onward VLA search window.
summary: PerAct encodes language goals and voxelized RGB-D observations with a Perceiver architecture. It learns discretized six-degree-of-freedom manipulation actions through behavior cloning.

name: ReKep (constraint-based planner)
title: ReKep: Spatio-Temporal Reasoning of Relational Keypoint Constraints for Robotic Manipulation
decision_reason: Keypoint constraints and trajectory optimization; contextual manipulation planner rather than a VLA action policy.
summary: ReKep uses visual-language reasoning to formulate relational constraints between task-relevant keypoints. It then optimizes robot motions to satisfy those constraints over time.

name: RT-1 (contextual precursor)
title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
decision_reason: Language-conditioned action-policy precursor first reported in 2022, outside January 2023 onward VLA search window.
summary: RT-1 maps camera observations and language instructions to discretized robot commands using a transformer policy. It is an early language-conditioned control precursor to later VLA foundation models.

name: SayCan (contextual planner)
title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
decision_reason: Language planner selects existing skills; not a unified learned visual-language action policy, and first report predates 2023.
summary: SayCan combines language-model task suggestions with learned skill-value estimates. It uses these estimates to select behaviors that are both instruction-relevant and physically feasible.

name: VIMA (contextual multimodal policy)
title: VIMA: General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts
decision_reason: Multimodal-prompt manipulation policy first reported in 2022, outside January 2023 onward VLA search window.
summary: VIMA specifies manipulation tasks using prompts that interleave text and images. A transformer policy converts these multimodal task descriptions and observations into robot actions.

name: VoxPoser (contextual planner)
title: VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models
decision_reason: VLM-generated value maps and motion planning are a modular control interface rather than the reviewed learned VLA policy class.
summary: VoxPoser converts language and visual information into composable three-dimensional value maps. These maps guide motion planning for manipulation instead of directly predicting motor commands from a single policy head.

name: AR-WAM
title: AR-WAM: A Visual-Conditioned Agent-Ready World Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
secondary_roles: WAM; agent interface; expanded search window; no language encoder
decision_reason: Adds a manipulation WAM with simulation and physical robot evaluations; it is not a VLA under a language-conditioned policy-interface criterion.
summary: AR-WAM conditions a predictive robot policy on a visual target and an operation token rather than a language encoder. It jointly predicts latent scene evolution and actions, with a separate agent interface handling longer task coordination.

name: AVDC
title: Learning to act from actionless videos through dense correspondences
decision_reason: Task-conditioned visual prediction is converted to robot control and evaluated on manipulation.
summary: AVDC generates task-directed videos and uses dense correspondences between frames to infer control actions. This connects action-free video demonstrations to robot execution.

name: Cosmos
title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
subtype: Video foundation model with robotic adaptation
secondary_roles: action-conditioned adaptation; data curation; video generation
decision_reason: Section 6.2 evaluates robot video prediction, including post-training for action-vector-conditioned next-frame generation.
summary: Cosmos provides video tokenizers, a curation pipeline and generative world foundation models. Its robotic post-training examples include instruction-conditioned video prediction and action-vector-conditioned next-frame prediction, distinct from an unadapted backbone.

name: Cosmos Policy
title: Cosmos Policy: Fine-tuning video models for visuomotor control and planning
subtype: World-action model with policy and planning modes
decision_reason: Manipulation policy jointly predicts actions, future state and value; direct control and rollout-based planning are separately evaluated.
summary: Cosmos Policy adapts a video model to jointly generate actions, future states, and values. It evaluates direct visuomotor execution alongside rollout refinement and candidate selection for planning.

name: Ctrl-World
title: Ctrl-World: A Controllable Generative World Model for Robot Manipulation
decision_reason: Provides controllable multi-view robot rollouts for policy evaluation and policy-improvement data.
summary: Ctrl-World predicts multi-view video under robot actions and retrieves pose-conditioned memory to extend rollout consistency. It uses generated trajectories for policy evaluation and corrective training, with evidence limited to the reported protocols.

name: DINO-WM
title: DINO-WM: World models on pre-trained visual features enable zero-shot planning
decision_reason: Learns transitions over pretrained visual features and evaluates visual goal-directed control, including manipulation.
summary: DINO-WM learns action-conditioned transitions over pretrained DINO image features. It plans toward visual goals in feature space without reconstructing future images.

name: DreamDojo
title: DreamDojo: A generalist robot world model from large-scale human videos
decision_reason: Adapts human-video pretraining to robot-action simulation and evaluates downstream robot uses.
summary: DreamDojo learns an action-conditioned video world model from human videos using continuous latent actions as proxy controls, then adapts it with robot data. Its generated rollouts support applications including policy evaluation and model-based planning.

name: DreamerV3
title: Mastering diverse control tasks through world models
secondary_roles: general-control foundation; model-based RL; simulated manipulation
decision_reason: Primary published report explicitly includes robot manipulation domains alongside locomotion and games.
summary: DreamerV3 learns policies through trajectories imagined in a latent dynamics model with training procedures shared across domains. The published evaluation spans robot manipulation and locomotion as well as games, so manipulation relevance should not be inferred solely from its Minecraft demonstration.

name: DreamGen
title: DreamGen: Unlocking generalization in robot learning through video world models
decision_reason: Generates robot video and inferred action labels and evaluates downstream manipulation-policy training.
summary: DreamGen generates task-conditioned robot videos and obtains pseudo-action labels through inverse dynamics. The resulting synthetic trajectories augment policy training as an offline data-generation pipeline.

name: DreamVLA
title: DreamVLA: A vision-language-action model dreamed with comprehensive world knowledge
decision_reason: Uses predicted dynamic, spatial and semantic information for manipulation action generation.
summary: DreamVLA forecasts compact dynamic, spatial, and semantic representations. A diffusion-based action generator conditions its manipulation commands on this predicted world information.

name: DreamZero
title: World action models are zero-shot policies
decision_reason: Joint future video and robot action generation is evaluated as a closed-loop manipulation policy.
summary: DreamZero jointly predicts future video and robot actions using a pretrained video-diffusion backbone. It uses this world-action representation for closed-loop control and studies transfer from heterogeneous robot data and video demonstrations.

name: FLARE — implicit world modeling
title: FLARE: Robot learning with implicit world modeling
decision_reason: Evaluates future-latent representation alignment for manipulation policies; prediction is an auxiliary mechanism.
summary: FLARE aligns policy features with embeddings of future observations to incorporate latent prediction into diffusion-based action learning. It also supports co-training with action-free video and is distinct from the reinforcement-learning method FLaRe.

name: FlowDreamer
title: FlowDreamer: A RGB-D World Model with Flow-based Motion Representations for Robot Manipulation
secondary_roles: 3D scene flow; geometric prediction; visual planning
decision_reason: Adds explicit action-conditioned geometric motion prediction with manipulation-control evaluation.
summary: FlowDreamer predicts three-dimensional scene flow from observations and robot actions before generating future RGB-D frames. Its experiments cover robot video prediction and visual planning.

name: Genie (first generation)
title: Genie: Generative interactive environments
secondary_roles: game-domain overlap; latent actions; robot video prediction
decision_reason: Beyond platformer experiments, Sec. 3.2 reports a robotics-trained model and controllable robot-object video prediction.
summary: Genie learns latent action codes and video dynamics from unlabelled videos. A robotics-trained variant predicts robot-object interactions under these latent controls, while the policy-transfer experiment in the paper concerns a game environment.

name: Genie Envisioner / GE-Base / GE-Act / GE-Sim
title: Genie envisioner: A unified world foundation platform for robotic manipulation
subtype: Unified video, policy and learned-simulation platform
secondary_roles: VLA overlap; WAM; learned simulation; policy evaluation
decision_reason: One paper contains GE-Base, GE-Act and GE-Sim and evaluates robotic manipulation functions.
summary: Genie Envisioner combines instruction-conditioned video prediction, action generation and learned simulation in GE-Base, GE-Act and GE-Sim. These components belong to one paper and must be counted once.

name: GR-1
title: Unleashing large-scale video generative pre-training for visual robot manipulation
decision_reason: Video-predictive pretraining and joint future-image/action prediction are evaluated on robotic manipulation.
summary: GR-1 predicts future images and robot actions from language, visual history, and robot state after video pretraining. This shared predictive-policy training is distinct from searching over supplied candidate actions during deployment.

name: GWM — Gaussian World Models
title: GWM: Towards scalable gaussian world models for robotic manipulation
decision_reason: Gaussian scene dynamics support robot outcome prediction and learned-simulator policy optimization.
summary: GWM models action-conditioned manipulation dynamics using Gaussian scene representations. The paper studies this representation for predictive pretraining and learned simulation.

name: HarmoWAM
title: HarmoWAM: Harmonizing generalizable and precise manipulation via adaptive world action models
subtype: Adaptive predictive and reactive world-action model
decision_reason: Evaluates coordinated predictive/reactive experts on physical manipulation tasks and unseen conditions.
summary: HarmoWAM combines predictive and reactive action experts through adaptive gating. This architecture aims to balance generalization with precise manipulation control.

name: IRASim
title: IRASim: A Fine-Grained World Model for Robot Manipulation
decision_reason: Adds an action-conditioned manipulation world model with policy-evaluation and planning experiments.
summary: IRASim conditions video diffusion on frame-aligned robot actions to model detailed robot-object interactions. It evaluates generated rollouts for policy assessment and visual model-based planning.

name: iVideoGPT
title: iVideoGPT: Interactive VideoGPTs are scalable world models
secondary_roles: action conditioning; model-based RL; video generation
decision_reason: Action-aware video modeling supports robot visual planning and model-based policy learning.
summary: iVideoGPT autoregressively models tokenized observations, actions, and rewards. Its learned dynamics support interactive video prediction, visual planning, and model-based reinforcement learning.

name: LaDi-WM
title: LaDi-WM: A Latent Diffusion-based World Model for Predictive Manipulation
secondary_roles: diffusion policy; latent prediction; real robot
decision_reason: Adds a manipulation-specific latent predictive model and downstream policy evaluation.
summary: LaDi-WM predicts future geometric and semantic features in a pretrained visual-feature space using latent diffusion. A robot policy incorporates these forecasts while refining actions, with simulated and physical manipulation evaluations.

name: LaWAM
title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies
decision_reason: Predicts latent subgoals to condition robot actions and evaluates simulation and real manipulation.
summary: LaWAM predicts latent visual subgoals and conditions robot-action generation on them. It incorporates predictive information into a policy without requiring dense future-image generation.

name: ManiGaussian
title: ManiGaussian: Dynamic gaussian splatting for multi-task robotic manipulation
decision_reason: Dynamic Gaussian reconstruction provides predictive supervision in RLBench manipulation.
summary: ManiGaussian uses dynamic Gaussian representations and future-scene reconstruction as predictive supervision for manipulation. Its language-conditioned policy evaluation is conducted in RLBench simulation.

name: ManipDreamer
title: ManipDreamer: Boosting Robotic Manipulation World Model with Action Tree and Visual Guidance
decision_reason: Adds a robot-world-model study with instruction structure and manipulation evaluation; linguistic action-tree nodes should not be mistaken for executable action vectors.
summary: ManipDreamer encodes relations among instruction primitives with an action tree and adds depth and semantic guidance to robot video prediction. It evaluates both generated-video quality and downstream RLBench manipulation.

name: RoboDream
title: RoboDream: Compositional World Models for Scalable Robot Data Synthesis
secondary_roles: embodiment conditioning; real robot; synthetic data
decision_reason: Adds manipulation evidence for world-model-based data generation and separates it from direct online planning.
summary: RoboDream anchors generated robot demonstrations to rendered robot motion while varying scene and object context. It evaluates whether the resulting synthetic data improves downstream real-world manipulation policies.

name: RoboDreamer
title: RoboDreamer: Learning Compositional World Models for Robot Imagination
decision_reason: Adds a manipulation-specific compositional predictive-planning approach absent from current citations.
summary: RoboDreamer decomposes language instructions into reusable primitives and composes the corresponding video-generation factors. It evaluates unseen compositional video plans and their execution in robot simulation.

name: StructVLA
title: Beyond Dense Futures: World Models as Structured Planners for Robotic Manipulation
subtype: Structured visual foresight for action policies
decision_reason: Trains sparse predictive milestones then adapts to low-level manipulation actions.
summary: StructVLA first trains a generative model to predict sparse visual milestones from instructions and observation history. A second training stage adapts that model to action-token prediction conditioned on instructions and interleaved observation–action history.

name: SuSIE
title: Zero-shot robotic manipulation with pretrained image-editing diffusion models
decision_reason: Image-editing diffusion proposes subgoals for a robot controller and is evaluated in manipulation.
summary: SuSIE adapts an image-editing diffusion model to propose visual subgoals from an observation and language instruction. A goal-conditioned controller executes the proposed subgoals.

name: Tactile-WAM
title: Tactile-WAM: Touch-Aware World Action Model with Tactile Asymmetric Attention
decision_reason: Joint visual/tactile/action modeling is evaluated on contact-rich simulation and real robot tasks.
summary: Tactile-WAM jointly models visual, tactile, and action information with tactile asymmetric attention. It directs contact information toward action prediction while limiting interference with video generation.

name: TD-MPC2
title: TD-MPC2: Scalable, robust world models for continuous control
decision_reason: Evaluates explicit manipulation suites Meta-World and ManiSkill2, including multi-object tasks.
summary: TD-MPC2 learns task-conditioned latent dynamics and value functions for model-predictive control. Its evaluation includes Meta-World and ManiSkill2 manipulation alongside other continuous-control domains.

name: TesserAct
title: TesserAct: Learning 4D embodied world models
decision_reason: Predicts scene geometry and appearance and connects these predictions to inverse-dynamics manipulation policies.
summary: TesserAct predicts RGB, depth, and surface-normal video to represent how three-dimensional scenes evolve. Its multimodal predictions also support learning inverse dynamics for embodied tasks.

name: TouchWorld
title: TouchWorld: A Predictive and Reactive Tactile Foundation Model for Dexterous Manipulation
subtype: Predictive and reactive tactile policy hierarchy
secondary_roles: VLA overlap; WAM; hierarchical control; tactile
decision_reason: Tactile world-model subgoals and fast residual control are evaluated in dexterous contact-rich manipulation.
summary: TouchWorld combines predicted tactile subgoals and visuomotor action chunks with a faster tactile and proprioceptive correction policy. This joins predictive and reactive control for contact-rich dexterous manipulation.

name: UniPi
title: Learning universal policies via text-guided video generation
decision_reason: Task-conditioned video generation plus inverse dynamics is evaluated for robot manipulation.
summary: UniPi generates a language-conditioned video plan and recovers executable actions through inverse dynamics. The generated plan is a visual action proposal rather than a forward prediction conditioned on supplied candidate robot actions.

name: UniSim
title: Learning interactive real-world simulators
decision_reason: Interactive video simulation supports robot learning and evaluation.
summary: UniSim learns an interactive video simulator that responds to high-level instructions or low-level controls. It supports policy learning and evaluation through generated environment interactions.

name: V-JEPA 2 / V-JEPA 2-AC
title: V-JEPA 2: Self-supervised video models enable understanding, prediction and planning
secondary_roles: action-conditioned adaptation; human video; latent planning
decision_reason: The same report presents action-free pretraining and V-JEPA 2-AC manipulation planning.
summary: V-JEPA 2 learns predictive representations through action-free video pretraining. The same paper introduces the action-conditioned V-JEPA 2-AC adaptation and evaluates image-goal planning for robot manipulation.

name: Video Language Planning (VLP)
title: Video language planning
decision_reason: Search over language and video plans is executed by a goal-conditioned manipulation policy.
summary: Video Language Planning searches over language proposals and generated video continuations using vision-language policies and value functions. A goal-conditioned policy executes the resulting visual plan.

name: VLA-JEPA
title: VLA-JEPA: Enhancing vision-language-action model with latent world model
decision_reason: Future-state representation targets improve VLA manipulation learning; future frames are supervision, not online prediction inputs.
summary: VLA-JEPA pretrains a policy backbone to predict future latent states from current observations. It subsequently adapts an action head, with future frames serving as training targets rather than inputs to the prediction pathway.

name: World-Gymnast
title: World-Gymnast: Training robots with reinforcement learning in a world model
subtype: Learned environment for robot reinforcement learning
secondary_roles: learned simulation; model-based RL; real robot transfer
decision_reason: Evaluates learned-world-model policy training and four-task transfer to physical robot manipulation.
summary: World-Gymnast trains robot policies with reinforcement learning inside a learned environment and tests transfer to hardware. Its physical-task comparisons provide evidence about the complete training-and-simulation package rather than isolating every component.

name: WorldEval / Policy2Vec
title: WorldEval: World model as real-world robot policies evaluator
decision_reason: WorldEval/Policy2Vec is a learned-simulation evaluation method for robot policies, not only a benchmark.
summary: WorldEval adapts video generation to action-following simulation using Policy2Vec. It evaluates robot policies through generated rollouts instead of requiring each evaluation to run on hardware.

name: WorldVLA
title: WorldVLA: Towards autoregressive action world model
decision_reason: Manipulation experiments evaluate joint predictive/action training and its ablations.
summary: WorldVLA uses shared autoregressive modeling for robot actions and future observations. Its predictive-training experiments provide evidence about joint learning without establishing a general advantage for online candidate-action search.

name: WoW / WoWBench
title: WoW: Towards a World omniscient World model Through Embodied Interaction
subtype: Robot-interaction video model with plan refinement
secondary_roles: Benchmark/dataset/evaluation overlap; inverse dynamics; video planning
decision_reason: Adds a robot-interaction world-model study; WoWBench is a secondary contribution in this same paper and must not create a second report count.
summary: WoW trains a generative world model on robot-interaction trajectories and uses a vision-language evaluator to refine proposed video plans. An inverse-dynamics model translates plans into actions, while the same paper introduces WoWBench for physical consistency.

name: Dreamer (first generation)
title: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination
decision_reason: Retained as historical general continuous-control context; not counted as a manipulation-focused report in the proposed core set.
summary: Dreamer learns a policy and value function from latent imagined trajectories, propagating gradients through predicted states. The original report is retained as general visual continuous-control background.

name: Dreamer 4
title: Training agents inside of scalable world models
decision_reason: Main control evidence is Minecraft; no direct robotic manipulation evaluation supports core inclusion.
summary: Dreamer 4 trains agents inside a scalable video world model learned from offline data. Its main application is Minecraft, while separate ablations examine the amount of action-labeled video required for prediction.

name: DreamerV2
title: Mastering Atari with Discrete World Models
decision_reason: Primary evaluation concerns Atari games rather than robotic manipulation.
summary: DreamerV2 learns behavior inside a world model with discrete latent states. Its main experiments use Atari games, making it historical context for this manipulation review.

name: Genie 2
title: Genie 2: A large-scale foundation world model
decision_reason: Official research announcement; no dedicated research paper is identified in this catalogue and no core manipulation evaluation is established.
summary: Genie 2 is an officially announced generator of interactive three-dimensional visual environments. The cited web announcement is kept separate from the paper count and from validated robot-manipulation evidence.

name: Genie 3
title: Genie 3: A new frontier for world models
decision_reason: Official release is not a separately identified research paper; robot manipulation evidence is not established here.
summary: Genie 3 is an officially announced interactive visual environment generator. The cited announcement does not constitute a dedicated manipulation research paper in this register.

name: I-JEPA — representation precursor
title: Self-supervised learning from images with a joint-embedding predictive architecture
decision_reason: Image-region representation learning has no temporal robot-action transition or manipulation-control evaluation.
summary: I-JEPA learns image representations by predicting target-region embeddings from visible context. It is a representation-learning precursor rather than a temporal, action-conditioned robot dynamics model.

name: MuZero
title: Mastering Atari, Go, chess and shogi by planning with a learned model
subtype: Latent decision model for game search
decision_reason: Primary evidence concerns board games and Atari, without robotic manipulation evaluation.
summary: MuZero learns latent transitions that predict rewards, values, and action priors for tree search. Its cited demonstrations concern games, with planning-relevant prediction that does not require observation reconstruction.

name: PhysDreamer
title: PhysDreamer: Physics-based interaction with 3D objects via video generation
decision_reason: Demonstrates elastic-object responses and perceptual realism, without downstream robot manipulation-control evaluation.
summary: PhysDreamer distills motion information from video generation into physical material estimates and interactive three-dimensional dynamics. Its object-response demonstrations provide context for physical prediction rather than direct evidence of robot task success.

name: PlaNet
title: Learning latent dynamics for planning from pixels
decision_reason: Retained as historical pixel-based continuous-control context rather than a manipulation-focused report in the proposed core set.
summary: PlaNet learns action-conditioned recurrent latent dynamics from images. It uses model-predictive control to select action sequences by evaluating imagined futures.

name: Sora — 2024 report
title: Video generation models as world simulators
decision_reason: Official web technical report on general video generation; retained as context rather than a dedicated manipulation research paper.
summary: The Sora technical report describes text-conditioned video generation and discusses emergent simulation properties and limitations. It is general video-model context rather than a robotic manipulation experiment.

name: UnifoLM-WMA-0
title: UnifoLM-WMA-0: A World-Model-Action (WMA) Framework under UnifoLM Family
decision_reason: Official repository describes manipulation simulation and policy modes, but identifies no dedicated research paper.
summary: UnifoLM-WMA-0 connects video-world-model prediction with robot action generation and an interactive simulation mode. Its official repository is retained as a software release because the inspected citation identifies no dedicated research paper.

name: V-JEPA — representation precursor
title: Revisiting feature prediction for learning visual representations from video
decision_reason: Video representation learning does not provide the robot-action-conditioned planning adaptation evaluated in the later V-JEPA 2 paper.
summary: V-JEPA learns video representations by predicting masked spatiotemporal features. Its action-free pretraining provides predictive representations without directly defining a robot-action-conditioned forward model.

name: World Models
title: World models
decision_reason: CarRacing and Doom establish historical learning-in-imagination context rather than manipulation evidence.
summary: World Models combines a variational image encoder, recurrent latent dynamics, and a compact controller. It demonstrates learning behavior within a learned environment in simulated control tasks.

name: AgiBot World Colosseo
title: AgiBot World Colosseo: A large-scale manipulation platform for scalable and intelligent embodied systems
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: AgiBot World combines a standardized robot-data collection platform with diverse manipulation trajectories. Its accompanying policy experiments study how data scale and coverage affect generalist robot learning.

name: BEHAVIOR-1K
title: BEHAVIOR-1K: A human-centered, embodied AI benchmark with 1,000 everyday activities and realistic simulation
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: BEHAVIOR-1K defines everyday household activities and supports them through the OmniGibson simulation environment. Its evaluation emphasizes long-horizon behavior and complex interaction with diverse objects and physical materials.

name: BridgeData V2
title: BridgeData V2: A dataset for robot learning at scale
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: BridgeData V2 provides diverse real-robot manipulation trajectories for scalable robot learning. It supports studying how training across tasks and environments affects policy generalization.

name: CALVIN
title: CALVIN: A benchmark for language-conditioned policy learning for long-horizon robot manipulation tasks
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: CALVIN evaluates language-conditioned policies on sequences of manipulation tasks in simulation. It emphasizes long-horizon execution and transfer to unfamiliar instructions, objects, and environments.

name: Colosseum V2
title: Colosseum V2: Benchmarking Generalization for Vision-Language-Action Models
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: Colosseum V2 evaluates manipulation policies under in-domain and shifted conditions across tasks and robot morphologies. It uses GPU-parallel simulation and paired physical checks to study how simulated generalization relates to real-world behavior.

name: DexMimicGen
title: DexMimicGen: Automated data generation for bimanual dexterous manipulation via imitation learning
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: DexMimicGen extends demonstration-based data generation to bimanual dexterous manipulation in simulation. It handles coordination between manipulators when synthesizing trajectories for imitation learning.

name: DROID
title: DROID: A large-scale in-the-wild robot manipulation dataset
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: DROID provides diverse real-world robot manipulation demonstrations collected across environments. It supports research on policy learning and generalization from robot observations and actions.

name: EWMBench
title: EWMBench: Evaluating Scene, Motion, and Semantic Quality in Embodied World Models
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: EWMBench evaluates generated robot-manipulation videos for scene consistency, motion correctness, and semantic alignment. It curates manipulation tasks from AgiBot World and provides trajectory-sensitive metrics, but does not by itself establish closed-loop control performance.

name: FurnitureBench
title: FurnitureBench: Reproducible real-world benchmark for long-horizon complex manipulation
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: FurnitureBench provides a reproducible physical benchmark for long-horizon furniture assembly. It includes demonstration data, standardized setup resources, and a corresponding simulator for studying manipulation learning.

name: GemBench / 3D-LOTUS
title: Towards Generalizable Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation: A Benchmark and LLM-guided 3D Policy
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: GemBench tests language-conditioned manipulation generalization across novel placements, objects, and longer task compositions. The same paper supplies 3D-LOTUS and a hierarchical 3D-LOTUS++ policy as baselines, so the benchmark and policies form one report.

name: LIBERO
title: LIBERO: Benchmarking knowledge transfer for lifelong robot learning
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: LIBERO provides simulated manipulation tasks and demonstrations for studying knowledge transfer in lifelong robot learning. Its task suites examine different transfer settings, policy designs, and effects of sequential learning.

name: LIBERO-Plus
title: LIBERO-Plus: In-depth robustness analysis of vision-language-action models
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: LIBERO-Plus probes manipulation policies with controlled changes to visual conditions, physical configurations, and language instructions. It examines whether high benchmark success persists under perturbations and whether policies reliably use language.

name: LIBERO-Safety
title: LIBERO-Safety: A comprehensive benchmark for physical and semantic safety in vision-language-action models
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: LIBERO-Safety procedurally generates safety-critical manipulation scenarios and accompanying collision-free demonstrations. It evaluates physical and semantic safety properties of embodied policies under task constraints.

name: ManipArena
title: ManipArena: Comprehensive real-world evaluation of reasoning-oriented generalist robot manipulation
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: ManipArena provides standardized physical manipulation evaluation with structured task variation and paired real-to-simulation environments. It compares generalist policy configurations while tracking generalization and subtask-level performance.

name: ManiSkill3
title: ManiSkill3: GPU parallelized robotics simulation and rendering for generalizable embodied AI
subtype: Simulation platform with benchmark tasks and data
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: ManiSkill3 provides GPU-parallelized robotics simulation and rendering for learning manipulation policies. It includes diverse environments, demonstration data, and training baselines to support scalable robot-learning experiments.

name: Meta-World
title: Meta-world: A benchmark and evaluation for multi-task and meta reinforcement learning
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: Meta-World provides a collection of simulated manipulation tasks for multi-task and meta-reinforcement learning. It enables evaluation of shared learning across tasks and adaptation to new task instances.

name: MimicGen
title: MimicGen: A data generation system for scalable robot learning using human demonstrations
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
summary: MimicGen transforms and recombines human demonstrations to generate additional robot trajectories in conventional simulation. It is a demonstration-expansion pipeline rather than a learned environment dynamics model.

name: Open X-Embodiment / RT-X
title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic learning datasets and RT-X models
decision_reason: Primary paper describes a manipulation dataset, benchmark, evaluation framework, or reusable data-generation resource within the review scope; proposed inclusion requires author adjudication.
